claims.text: The tested material is HfNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy in an as-cast or annealed condition.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy contains inherent lattice distortions.
The inherent lattice distortions arise from high mixing entropy.
Diffusion-controlled recovery mechanisms are expected to be active between approximately 400°C and 1000°C.
Elevated temperature supplies sufficient thermal energy to activate dynamic recovery in HfNbTaTiZr.
Dynamic recovery and dislocation rearrangement reduce local lattice distortions.
Reduction of lattice distortion diminishes solution strengthening.
Between approximately 400°C and 1000°C, yield strength will be lower than at room temperature.
Between approximately 400°C and 1000°C, ultimate tensile strength will be lower than at room temperature.
Between approximately 400°C and 1000°C, the effective coefficient of thermal expansion will be higher than its room-temperature baseline.
Between approximately 400°C and 1000°C, elastic modulus will be lower than at room temperature.
The predicted responses apply in the elastic and early plastic deformation regimes before phase instability or other competing phenomena become dominant.
Changes in X-ray diffraction peak broadening or narrowing can be used to monitor changes in lattice distortion.
A reduction in lattice distortion should correlate with lower yield strength and elastic modulus and with higher thermal expansion.
